comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Measured rather than inferred: 2 failures in 30 runs of the test alone on an idle 10-core M-series laptop, and 0 in 20 earlier runs including 10 under twelve spinning cores. So load is not what decides it - the two events are simply close together. CI failed it twice in a row on a commit that changed only version strings, and its parent passed the gate first attempt four hours earlier, so the runner's rate is much higher than 7%.

The failing run takes 0.60s locally against CI's 0.41s and 0.49s, which is the shape of a race lost early rather than a deadline waited out.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`confirm_it_arrived` (crates/muster-seam/src/handler.rs:1580) reads the pane back exactly once, immediately after the daemon accepts the send. There is no wait and no retry. A send is accepted when the daemon has taken the bytes, which is before the program in the pane has read them, echoed them, and had the result land in the daemon's copy of the screen. So the read can arrive first, find no text, and `--confirm` refuses a message that did arrive.

## How it showed up

The gate went red on CI for v0.7.0 on a commit that changed nothing but version strings - `a_send_the_pane_never_showed_is_refused_rather_than_reported_as_done` (crates/muster-seam/tests/confirmed_send.rs) failed on the FIRST of its three sends, the short `hello` that the fixture is built to draw whole. The failure text was "the text was sent to pane p21yn7s178 and is not on it", which is the `Ok(_)` arm at handler.rs:1584: the read succeeded and simply did not contain the text yet. Not the `Err` arm, so not a timeout - this is the read winning the race.

Ten local runs on an unloaded machine were green, and the same code passed CI one commit earlier. So it takes a loaded machine, which is exactly the machine an agent driving several panes at once is running on.

## Why it is worth a card

This is the false negative the flag was built to make impossible. A caller reads exit 1 and concludes the agent never got the message, so it sends again - and the agent gets the brief twice, or the caller escalates to a person over a message that landed fine.

Distinct from a_2LOHfLmsL, which is worth saying because both read as "a delivered message reported as refused". That one is a 500ms timeout at the Muster-to-herdr seam turned into an assertion that nothing moved; the answer was lost. This one has no lost answer anywhere: every request succeeded, and the read was simply taken too early.

## A shape for the fix

Give the read-back a deadline rather than a single shot: re-read until the text is found or a budget runs out, and refuse only then. That keeps the fast path free - a pane that has already drawn the text answers on the first read, which is the common case - and costs a genuine miss the budget rather than costing every caller a false refusal.

What the budget should be is the real question, and it is the same one the ten-second painting watch answered: how long may an honest pane take to draw what it was handed. It wants to be argued from a measurement rather than picked, and the test's own fixture is a place to take one.
title: muster pane send --confirm reads the pane back before it can have drawn
